evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Jeline: 'I just have a few questions to give you the accurate code. I just need ten to fifteen minutes of your time, if that's okay?' — Time-boxed but missing explicit promise of dependable quote; no real wait for confirmation before moving to concerns.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Jeline: 'Before I proceed aside from the pricing Trevor, do you have any other concern about the moving process?' — Asked, but after the introduction; Trevor answered 'Not really,' so technically no concerns raised. However, phrasing is closer to their-agenda intent than it appears at first read, though it comes after the quid-pro-quo setup rather than cleanly before probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — Trevor raised no concerns to follow up on; he stated 'Not really' when asked.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — No concerns were raised, so reflection was not applicable.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Jeline confirmed: pickup address (6202 Drive, San Antonio 78238), property type (apartment), floor/stories (second floor, no elevator), rooms (1 bedroom + den area), walking distance (balcony/den clarified), additional stops (destination: 27 Messenger Creek, 1700 sq ft, 2-story house), special considerations (stairs access, TV size 55 inches, guitars, racing simulator, valuable items itemized), parking (confirmed at destination). All seven logistics items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Jeline did not ask 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' — the customer brought up unpacking help unprompted, and Jeline clarified what services are and are not available, but never offered packing as a service.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Jeline: 'For an apartment your size we 15 to 25 boxes do you think you would fall within that range or do you have a large collection that could possibly put you out of that range?' — Box count range provided and overflow check performed.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Jeline: '$96 per hour, per mover... two mover for this move... $192... estimated cost for your move is between $672 to $2,864.' — Range given with time estimate (3.5–4.5 hours, 2 movers, 1 truck) and typical-for-size anchor. Minimal personalization to Trevor's stated concerns (stairs, second floor destination); mention of furniture assembly help is light personalization tied to the route complexity, but not explicitly tied to his move profile.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Jeline: 'everything is included... gas and truck taxes, insurance... we will just wrap your furniture with shin craps and moving blanks... minimum of two and a half hours... time is prorated in fifteen minute increments.' — Fee transparency and commitment framing both present. No explicit 'not a guess' language, but the prorated/minimum structure is stated.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Jeline does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' She transitions directly: 'So with that, would you like to be on the schedule for October 5th...' — No feelings check, no silence hold.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Not mentioned. Jeline provides no version of the On-Time Guarantee (discount terms if late).
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Not mentioned. Jeline provides no version of No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000 coverage, no deductible, built into rate).
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Jeline does not explicitly close the Two Promises loop. She moves directly from pricing estimate to booking attempt.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Jeline: 'Mm-hmm anything else I can do for you today?' — This is the throwaway 'anything else' phrasing, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you?' or deeper check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Jeline does not ask a catch-all like 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' She jumps to the closing question.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Jeline never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent. She asks 'So with that, would you like to be on the schedule for October 5th...' but when Trevor expresses hesitation ('I just want to get a quote, I might do, I might do a week later'), she pivots immediately to 'I can just send you the estimate details to your email and then if you're ready to book you could just reply to my email or give us a call' — a built-in out, no re-ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. Jeline does not reference rate-lock or no-deposit as a reason to book now.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Jeline confirms: date (October 5th), arrival window (8:30–9:00 AM), no deposit required. She does NOT confirm: phone number, crew size (mentioned 2 movers, 1 truck in estimate but not re-confirmed in booking), addresses (pickup and destination mentioned earlier but not re-confirmed in booking summary), or notes left for crew about concerns. The booking was not completed because Trevor declined and asked for email estimate instead.

top_strength: Jeline thoroughly gathered logistics details—property type, floor/stories, room count, walking distances, special items, and valuables—ensuring the estimate would be accurate and informed.
coaching_note: The call lacks the two critical selling moments: never deliver the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage), and never ask a genuine explicit close ('Would you like our help?') with a real pause—instead pivot away to an out the moment the customer hesitates.
